questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some of the most crucial aspects of choosing my destination were the language, culture, and personal interests. My chosen country was Soth Korea, and I began involved in the culture during Covid which motivated me to learn the language and my interest to experience the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some parts didn't work out well, but overall I had a really amazing experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. At first, it was a bit difficult to navigate the website of my exchange university, however, some of their services helped a lot. You have to be prepared to double-check everything, to make sure everything is in order.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At Korea University they had a Global service center which helped a lot in terms of practical information and course registration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit hard at first cause the university didn't offer that much help in terms of off-campus accommodation. I recommend using Goshipages, a website for small affordable student rooms. They often have goshiwons (rooms) near universities so it is fairly easy to find. If you are going to Sungkyeongkwan Uni or Korea university I recommend staying at 'Ciel house', which can be found on the goshipages.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You should plan far in advance if you want off-campus accommodation!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some goshiwons (rooms) have a bad reputation and are very dirty so it is important to check if everything is proper, also in terms of the landlord, contact, and payment method.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a long process because you have to give a lot of information and prepare a lot of documents to get accepted. Be sure to read everything twice or more to ensure you send everything the host university need to evaluate your application.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always mail home the university about the process if something is unclear, however, if you just read thoroughly it all makes sense.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At Korea University it was a bit hard to find courses that fit all the requirements of the home university and in the first registration period, you have to be prepared on the dot to get spots on the courses you want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ensure that you know the specific time of the first registration period. You may have to wake up at night or early morning for registration of courses. Have a few back up courses as well, because you may not get a spot on some of the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: At Korea univeristy the academic level was pretty high since it is one of the top univeristies in South Korea. However, the courses were very interesting which motivated me to work hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style involved a lot of discussions that motivated students to participate in class. In my courses, we had research projects in groups which gave us the opportunity to get to know each better and explore and go in-depth with a specific theme.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Media and Gender, Media technologies and culture, Theories of media effects, Mass media and popular culture in Korea, and Korean society and culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend choosing courses that are relevant to your field and combining Korean culture courses which can enhance knowledge about the country and its history and culture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Did not encounter anything unexpected, however, I changed my accommodation once during the 4,5 months a spent there, which meant that my rent increased a bit.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything in Korea is less expensive compared to Denmark, especially transportation. Clothes and food were affordable as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in any of the clubs at the host university, and I heard that some clubs were hard to get into.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had several sports clubs like football, badminton, and dance. I don't feel like they promoted the clubs very well and for me it was hard to obtain information about the clubs available on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Exploring different parts of the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting other cities such as Busan and Jeju Island. There are so many diverse activities in Seoul and many cafés that offer different activities such as painting or making your own phone covers. You have to try noraebang which is karaoke!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn't hard. The first few days you learn the customs and you get used to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be involved in clubs and your KUBA group which will be assigned to you at orientation!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: When you are a foreigner in Korea people tend to look at you more (mostly older citizens), however, most people were very sweet.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and the Korean pop culture (k-pop).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be sure to plan everything far in advance, work load  might be higher, and be involved in your KUBA groups social activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of all the deadlines when applying for the exchange program as well as the courses you need to enlist in.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends and experiencing all the amazing activities and spots in Seoul

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had five courses which was a bit much and a bit stressful at times, however, it is required when applying as an undergraduate student

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
